name: Microsoft Outlook (Microsoft Graph / Entra ID)
verdict: Register a multitenant Entra app with delegated Mail.Read/Mail.Send plus offline_access. You will have a working token in about 20 minutes, but get publisher verification through the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program before launch: unverified multitenant apps are stepped up to admin consent in most business tenants, and expect most business tenants to need admin consent for Mail.Read anyway: since late 2025 the Microsoft-managed default consent policy (default for new tenants) excludes Mail.Read/ReadWrite/ReadBasic, Calendars.*, Chat.* and IMAP/EWS from user consent, even for verified publishers. Mail.Send alone remains user-consentable.

difficulty.label: Moderate
difficulty.rationale: Microsoft runs no app-review queue for Graph mail scopes. The practical gate is publisher verification, which needs a verified Partner Center (AI Cloud Partner Program) account (business, domain, employment and identity checks, typically 3–5 business days). The other gate is tenant admin consent policies that you do not control. Since Oct–Nov 2025 (MC1163922) tenants on the Microsoft-managed consent policy require admin consent for delegated mailbox-read permissions regardless of publisher verification, so admin consent is the norm for read-mail agents.

first_token.note: Entra admin center > App registrations > New registration, add a Web redirect URI and client secret, add delegated Mail.Read, Mail.Send and offline_access, then run the auth code flow against /common/oauth2/v2.0. Works immediately for your own tenant and personal Microsoft accounts.

production.estimate: 1–2 weeks (plus per-customer admin consent time, which can be days to months)
production.waiting: Partner Center account verification typically takes 3–5 business days and can run longer if documents are requested. Linking the Partner ID to the app takes minutes.
production.note: Driven by AI Cloud Partner Program enrollment and verification (legal business docs, domain registrar documentation, employment check) and by each enterprise customer's consent policy. Many tenants require an admin to approve any third-party app.

cost: Free. App registration, publisher verification and the AI Cloud Partner Program basic membership have no fee. Microsoft 365 App Certification is optional and paid to an audit firm.

paths.name: Single tenant (AzureADMyOrg)
paths.who_for: Internal agents for your own organization
paths.review: none. A tenant admin can grant consent directly.
paths.limits: Only users in your directory can sign in.

paths.name: Multitenant + personal accounts (AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount)
paths.who_for: Public agent products where both work/school Outlook and Outlook.com/Hotmail users connect
paths.review: No Microsoft review. Publisher verification is strongly recommended, but it does not unlock user consent for Mail.Read in tenants on the Microsoft-managed default policy (admin consent required there).
paths.limits: Unverified: risk-based step-up blocks user consent for non-basic scopes in tenants that allow user consent, so users see AADSTS90094 or an admin-request flow. Personal-account configs allow 100 redirect URIs, no wildcards and no query strings, and at most 2 client secrets.

paths.name: Multitenant work/school only (AzureADMultipleOrgs)
paths.who_for: B2B agents targeting Microsoft 365 business customers only
paths.limits: Up to 256 redirect URIs. Customer admin consent is often required by tenant policy.

prerequisites.item: A Microsoft Entra tenant with a work/school account (not a personal MSA)
prerequisites.note: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account cannot be publisher verified.

prerequisites.item: A custom domain verified in the tenant (DNS TXT) and set as the app's Publisher domain
prerequisites.note: *.onmicrosoft.com is not accepted for publisher verification.

prerequisites.item: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (Partner Center) account, fully verified, using the Partner Global Account (PGA) Partner One ID
prerequisites.note: Needs a business email on the same domain, business registration documents, and domain registrar documentation.

prerequisites.item: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator role in Entra; Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center; MFA enabled
Privacy statement and terms of service URLs, and an app logo
prerequisites.note: Shown on the consent prompt via Branding & properties.

steps.title: Create the app registration
steps.detail: entra.microsoft.com > Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Name: your product name. Supported account types: 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' for broad reach, or 'Accounts in any organizational directory' for B2B only. Redirect URI: platform 'Web', e.g. https://app.example.com/oauth/microsoft/callback. Click Register and copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID.

steps.title: Add a credential
steps.detail: Certificates & secrets > Client secrets > New client secret. Choose an expiry (the portal caps it at 24 months; the recommended default is 180 days). Copy the Value immediately because it is shown once. For production, prefer a certificate or federated credential and automate rotation before expiry.

steps.title: Add delegated Graph permissions
steps.detail: API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions: openid, profile, email, offline_access, User.Read, Mail.Read (or Mail.ReadBasic / Mail.ReadWrite), and Mail.Send. Avoid Application permissions (Mail.Read app-only), which always need admin consent and grant access to every mailbox. Do not click 'Grant admin consent' unless you mean it for your own tenant.

steps.title: Branding & properties
steps.detail: Set Name, Logo, Home page URL, Terms of service URL, Privacy statement URL. Under Publisher domain, select 'Update domain' and pick your DNS-verified custom domain.

steps.title: Run the auth code flow
steps.detail: GET https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&redirect_uri=...&response_mode=query&scope=offline_access%20User.Read%20Mail.Read%20Mail.Send&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256. POST the code to https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token with client_secret and code_verifier. Call GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages.

steps.title: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program
steps.detail: partner.microsoft.com > Join the AI Cloud Partner Program, signing in with an account in the same tenant as the app. Complete the email, identity, employment and business verification checks (Partner Center > Account settings > Verification summary). Upload incorporation documents and domain registrar documentation if asked.
steps.wait: 3–5 business days typical; longer if more documents are requested

steps.title: Mark the app publisher verified
steps.detail: App registrations > your app > Branding & properties > 'Add Partner ID to verify publisher'. Enter the PartnerGlobal Partner One ID (from Partner Center > Account settings > Identifiers > Microsoft Cloud Partners Program) > Verify and save. Sign in with MFA. A blue verified badge appears next to Publisher display name within minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the admin-consent path for enterprise customers
steps.detail: Publish an admin-consent link: https://login.microsoftonline.com/{customer-tenant-id or organizations}/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=...&scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.Read https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.Send offline_access&redirect_uri=...&state=.... Write a short IT-admin doc listing each permission and why it is needed.

steps.title: Optional: Microsoft 365 Publisher Attestation / Certification
steps.detail: Partner Center > Microsoft 365 App Compliance. Publisher Attestation is a self-assessed questionnaire. Certification is an independent audit (annual) and helps with security-conscious enterprise admins. Neither is required to function.
steps.wait: Certification: 14-day document stage plus 60-day evidence review

review.trigger: No Microsoft app review exists for Graph delegated mail scopes. Effective gates: (1) publisher verification, needed to avoid risk-based step-up for multitenant apps and to qualify under 'verified publishers only' consent policies; (2) each customer tenant's user-consent policy and admin approval. (3) Since late 2025, the Microsoft-managed default consent policy requires admin consent for delegated mailbox/calendar/chat read permissions in tenants that use it.
review.process: Publisher verification is self-serve once your AI Cloud Partner Program account passes Microsoft's business verification. Per-tenant, admins grant consent through the admin consent endpoint, the Enterprise applications blade, or the admin consent request workflow.
review.typical_wait: Partner Center verification typically takes 3–5 business days (official). Linking the Partner ID takes minutes. Customer admin approval depends on the organization's IT process.
reviewers_check: Partner Center: business email domain, legal business registration, domain registrar docs, employment, government ID
Publisher domain matches the Partner Center primary contact email domain or a DNS-verified tenant domain
Customer IT admins check permission breadth (delegated vs application), verified badge, privacy/terms URLs, and certification status
common_rejections: MPNGlobalAccountNotFound: used a location Partner ID instead of PartnerGlobal
PublisherDomainMismatch: Partner Center email domain does not match the app's publisher domain
MSANotSupported: app registered under a personal Microsoft account
MPNAccountNotVetted: Partner Center verification still pending
Customer admins decline apps requesting Mail.ReadWrite or application permissions when read-only delegated access would suffice

pre_approval_limits: Tenants on the Microsoft-managed user consent policy ('Let Microsoft manage your consent settings', default for new tenants): users cannot consent to Mail.Read/ReadWrite/ReadBasic, Calendars.*, Chat.* or EWS/IMAP/POP/EAS for third-party apps, verified or not (rollout Oct–Nov 2025, MC1163922). Existing consents keep working.

Unverified multitenant app (registered after Nov 8, 2020) requesting non-basic scopes: user consent is stepped up to admin consent in tenants with user consent enabled (risk-based step-up is on by default), and users see AADSTS90094 or a 'request approval' prompt
Tenants using microsoft-user-default-low allow user consent only for verified publishers' apps and low-impact permissions
Tenants with user consent disabled require admin consent for every third-party app, verified or not
Consent prompt shows 'unverified' publisher warning until verified

oauth.refresh_tokens: Issued only when offline_access is requested. Default Max Inactive Time is 90 days (sliding: each use issues a new refresh token, so discard the old one). SPA-type redirect URIs get 24-hour refresh tokens. Revoked on password reset, admin revocation, or by Conditional Access/CAE events. Lifetimes are not configurable since Jan 30, 2021.
oauth.access_token_lifetime: Random 60–90 minutes (75 average). Can be up to about 24–28 hours with Continuous Access Evaluation-capable clients.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: HTTPS required except localhost (http://localhost, where the port is ignored when matching). Exact, case-sensitive match. Maximum 256 characters per URI. Up to 256 URIs for org-only apps, 100 when personal accounts are included. Wildcards only for work/school-only apps via the manifest (not recommended). No query strings when personal accounts are supported. No special characters ! $ ' ( ) , ; and no IDNs. Platform type matters: Web vs SPA vs Mobile/desktop.
oauth.scopes: Delegated Graph scopes are requested as Mail.Read or https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.Read. Mail.Send (delegated) is user-consentable. Mail.ReadBasic, Mail.Read and Mail.ReadWrite are flagged user-consentable in Graph, but the Microsoft-managed default consent policy (default for new tenants; updated Oct–Nov 2025) excludes them, plus Calendars.*, Chat.*, Contacts.ReadWrite and EWS/IMAP/POP/EAS, from user consent, so those need admin consent in such tenants. Application permissions (app-only) always need admin consent. Dynamic/incremental consent is supported. /.default requests all statically configured permissions.
oauth.tenant_notes: Use /common for mixed account types and /organizations for work/school only. After consent, a service principal (Enterprise application) is created in each customer tenant. Use the 'tid' claim to key tokens per tenant. Admin consent: /{tenant}/v2.0/adminconsent (do not use 'common'). Guest users need the resource tenant ID, not common.

gotchas.title: Unverified multitenant apps are stepped up to admin consent
gotchas.detail: Risk-based step-up consent is on by default. For multitenant apps registered after Nov 2020 that are not publisher verified and request non-basic permissions (Mail.Read counts), user consent becomes an admin-consent requirement. Users hit AADSTS90094 unless the tenant has the admin consent workflow enabled.

gotchas.title: Many enterprise tenants disable user consent entirely
gotchas.detail: Microsoft recommends allowing user consent only for verified publishers and low-impact permissions. Many tenants disable it outright. Your onboarding must include an admin-consent link and IT-facing docs even when you are verified.

gotchas.title: Publisher verification needs a verified Partner Center business account
gotchas.detail: You need the PartnerGlobal (PGA) Partner One ID, an app registered in an Entra tenant linked to the PGA, a non-onmicrosoft publisher domain matching your Partner Center email domain, and MFA. Partner Center business verification usually takes 3–5 business days. Start it on day one.

gotchas.title: Client secrets expire (portal max 24 months)
gotchas.detail: Secrets created in the portal cap at 24 months, and a forgotten expiry takes every customer connection down at once. Monitor expiry, keep two overlapping secrets, rotate, or use certificates. Org policies may cap lifetimes further.

gotchas.title: offline_access is required for refresh tokens
gotchas.detail: Without offline_access in the scope string, no refresh_token is returned and the agent loses access after about 75 minutes.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens die after 90 days of inactivity
gotchas.detail: If an agent does not touch a user's connection for 90 days, the refresh token expires and the user must reconnect. Refresh periodically and always store the newest refresh token.

gotchas.title: Personal-account support restricts configuration
gotchas.detail: Including personal Microsoft accounts limits you to 100 redirect URIs, no wildcards or query strings, at most 2 client secrets, and 30 permissions per resource.

gotchas.title: Default consent policy now blocks user consent to Mail.Read
gotchas.detail: Since an Oct–Nov 2025 rollout (MC1163922), tenants using the Microsoft-managed user consent policy (the default for new tenants) require admin consent for third-party apps requesting Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.ReadBasic, Calendars.*, Chat.*, OnlineMeetings.*, Contacts.ReadWrite, People.Read and EWS/IMAP/POP/EAS, even from verified publishers. Mail.Send is not on the list. Earlier (mid-2025) the same policy excluded Files/Sites (MC1097272). Plan an admin-consent onboarding path (adminconsent link, admin consent workflow) for any read-mail agent.

blockers.symptom: AADSTS90094: <app> needs permission to access resources in your organization that only an admin can grant.
blockers.cause: Tenant requires admin consent (user consent disabled, Microsoft-managed default policy excluding Mail.Read and other mailbox scopes, or risk-based step-up for an unverified publisher)
blockers.fix: Send the customer's admin the /{tenant}/v2.0/adminconsent link, or ask them to enable the admin consent request workflow. Publisher verification helps only for the step-up case.

blockers.symptom: AADSTS65001: The user or administrator has not consented to use the application
blockers.cause: Requested scope not yet consented (for example, a newly added Mail.Send)
blockers.fix: Re-run the authorization with the new scope (incremental consent), or have an admin re-consent.

blockers.symptom: AADSTS50011: The redirect URI ... does not match the redirect URIs configured for the application
blockers.cause: URI mismatch or wrong platform type
blockers.fix: Add the exact URI under Authentication > Web platform. Check case, trailing slash, and http vs https.

blockers.symptom: AADSTS7000215: Invalid client secret provided / AADSTS7000222: client secret keys are expired
blockers.cause: Wrong secret (you used the Secret ID instead of the Value) or an expired secret
blockers.fix: Create a new secret, deploy it, then delete the old one.

blockers.symptom: Consent screen shows 'unverified' next to the publisher
blockers.fix: Branding & properties > Add Partner ID to verify publisher.

blockers.cause: Tenant not linked to the PGA, wrong role, or email domain mismatch
blockers.fix: Link the tenant in Partner Center, use the PartnerGlobal ID, and set the publisher domain to the domain of the Partner Center primary contact email.

agent_can: Choose minimal delegated scopes (Mail.ReadBasic vs Mail.Read vs Mail.ReadWrite)
Generate the app manifest and redirect URIs
Build the authorize, token and admin-consent URLs
Implement PKCE, offline_access, token rotation and per-tenant storage
Draft the privacy statement and terms
Script publisher verification via Graph setVerifiedPublisher once a human has the Partner ID
human_must: Sign in to Entra with MFA and an admin role
Verify the custom domain via DNS
Enroll in Partner Center and pass business, identity and employment verification
Upload legal business and domain documents
Click Verify and save for the Partner ID
Contact customer IT admins for consent

evidence.claim: Publisher verification requirements (PGA Partner One ID, publisher domain not onmicrosoft, MFA); free; minutes if prerequisites met; Nov 2020 consent change for unverified multitenant apps
evidence.note: Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification

evidence.claim: Risk-based step-up consent enabled by default; unverified multitenant nonbasic requests stepped up; AADSTS90094
evidence.note: This step-up capability is enabled by default | Re-checked 2026-10-30; applies to newly registered unverified multitenant apps

evidence.claim: User consent policies: microsoft-user-default-low (verified publishers, low impact) vs legacy; Microsoft recommends verified-publisher-only
evidence.note: allow user consent only for applications that have been published by a verified publisher

evidence.claim: Locked-down tenants can gate even delegated scopes behind admin approval
evidence.note: an administrator can still gate even delegated scopes

evidence.claim: Partner Center verification typically 3-5 business days; email/identity/employment/business checks
evidence.note: In most cases, the process takes three to five business days

evidence.claim: Publisher verification error codes and fixes
Portal client secret expiry capped at 24 months; PowerShell can exceed; policies can restrict
evidence.note: maximum of 24 months for the expiration of client secrets

evidence.claim: Microsoft recommends certificates over client secrets for production
evidence.note: recommends that you use a certificate instead of a client secret

evidence.claim: Endpoints, tenant values, PKCE recommended for all and required for SPA; refresh token only with offline_access; discard old refresh token; SPA 24h
evidence.note: Only provided if offline_access scope was requested

evidence.claim: Refresh token Max Inactive Time 90 days; not configurable since Jan 30 2021; access token 60-90 min
evidence.note: random value ranging between 60-90 minutes | Re-checked 2026-10-30

evidence.claim: Redirect URI limits: 256 vs 100 URIs, 256 chars, https except localhost, wildcards/query restrictions
evidence.note: You can use a maximum of 256 characters for each redirect URI

evidence.claim: Supported account types and consumer limits (max two client secrets, 30 perms per resource)
evidence.note: Maximum of two client secrets for consumer-inclusive types

evidence.claim: Microsoft-managed policy requiring admin consent for third-party file/site access, rollout Jul-Aug 2025 (MC1097272)
evidence.note: require administrator consent for third-party apps that access files and sites

evidence.claim: Admin consent endpoint format; do not use common
Microsoft 365 Certification is voluntary, annual, audited (14-day + 60-day stages)
evidence.note: Stage 2 Full Evidence Review: 60 day time frame

evidence.claim: Mark-as-verified portal steps (Branding & properties > Add Partner ID to verify publisher)

Microsoft-managed policy (microsoft-user-default-recommended, default for new tenants) lets users consent to delegated permissions EXCEPT Files/Sites .All, Mail.Read/ReadWrite/ReadBasic(+Shared), MailboxSettings, Calendars.*, Chat.*, OnlineMeetings.*, Contacts, Tasks, People.Read, EAS/EWS/IMAP/POP
evidence.note: "End users can consent for any user consentable delegated permissions EXCEPT:" (page updated 2026)

evidence.claim: MC1163922: admin approval required for third-party apps accessing Exchange/Teams content via delegated permissions in tenants on the Microsoft-managed policy; rollout end Oct to late Nov 2025; existing consents unaffected
evidence.note: Mirror of Microsoft 365 Message Center post; corroborated by learn.microsoft.com e17 and m365admin.handsontek.net

uncertain: Exact 'Admin consent required' flags for delegated Mail.Read/Mail.Send: the Graph permissions reference page was truncated when fetched; the 'No' (user-consentable) value is based on general knowledge plus a community source.
The 24-month portal cap on client secrets comes from a community source; the official credentials page did not state it.
The share of enterprise tenants that disable user consent is not published; 'many' is a qualitative judgement.
Partner Center verification can exceed 5 business days when extra documentation is requested; I found no reliable community distribution of wait times.

Share of customer tenants still on the Microsoft-managed default consent policy (vs custom or legacy policies) is not published; the excluded-permission list is auto-updated by Microsoft and may grow.

probes.what: /common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize with all-zero GUID client_id, scope Mail.Read offline_access
probes.result: AADSTS700038: <id> is not a valid application identifier
probes.method: Live browser request (no account created, no credentials used)
